en0: Everybody watched his right hand. Nobody watched his left.
He came from Benjamin, the tribe whose very name means son of the right hand. And God chose the man who was left-handed.
The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord. And for eighteen years, Eglon the king of Moab ruled over them.
Every year they carried a heavy tribute to his palace. And Eglon, the Bible says, was a very fat man.
And when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord raised them up a deliverer.
Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded.
en1: Ehud made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length. And he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh.
The guards searched the left side, where a right-handed man carries his blade. They never checked the right.
When the tribute was paid, Ehud sent the people home. Then he turned back. Alone.
And all that stood by him went out from him. The king sat alone in his cool summer parlour.
Eglon rose up out of his seat. And Ehud put forth his left hand. That day, God's judgment fell on the king of Moab.
Ehud shut the doors of the parlour upon him, and locked them, and slipped away through the porch.
en2: So they waited... till they were ashamed. And by the time they opened those doors, Ehud was long gone.
He blew a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.
Eighty years of peace. Started by the hand everybody overlooked.
